research.competitor_pattern: Public ChatGPT competitors remain easy to copy at the one-shot layer: MOG.EXE and multiple skincare GPTs center on scoring/advice. Larger adjacent apps differentiate with persistence and workflow: Flaired emphasizes learned taste/profile and wardrobe context; Thea combines face/routine analysis with product matching and progress; Sumi and Complexion emphasize longitudinal skin/routine history. Celebrity lookalike products remain highly shareable and event-driven.
research.public_signals: Current public App Store pages observed Thea with 13K ratings and Celebs celebrity-lookalike with 174K ratings; these are platform rating counts, not Rate My Face traction and not direct conversion evidence.
research.expansion_opportunity: Build a separate Style Evolution / lookalike-inspiration surface around consented history, saved looks, feedback and shareable comparisons rather than a generic celebrity identity matcher. Reuse the Rate My Face account layer; keep actual person identification out of the core face-analysis policy.

daily_reports.summary: Implemented Stripe-hosted subscription checkout, billing portal, webhook-driven entitlements, and premium-gated persistent memory. Production activation still requires Stripe configuration verification.
Verified Personal Network deployment and aligned the credit-metered Action architecture. Retention, GPT usage, Associates conversion and end-to-end credit metrics remained unmeasured.

Live closure review found production auth/database/Stripe secret/credit price/webhook configuration healthy, but zero Stripe Checkout Sessions and zero credit-ledger activity. Fixed and deployed a latent Personal Network recommendation-table collision. Public research supports longitudinal personalization/history and shareable comparison over one-shot face scoring. Critical remaining security issue: nine core product/billing tables have RLS disabled. PR #16 proposing 100 free signup credits remains unmerged pending explicit product approval.
